item.title: Quantum 6j-symbols arising from a subfactor of finite index and finite depth and the zipper condition for 4-tensors in two-dimensional topological order
item.description: arXiv:2611.02582v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study 3-tensors satisfying the ``zipper condition,'' which play an important role in tensor network approaches to two-dimensional topological order. In our previous work, we identified the 4-tensors appearing in these approaches with bi-unitary connections in the Jones theory of subfactors in operator algebras. These bi-unitary connections give rise to subfactors of finite index. We prove that, when the associated subfactor has finite depth, the 3-tensors satisfying the zipper condition correspond precisely to the quantum $6j$-symbols, also known as $F$-symbols, of the unitary multi-fusion category arising from the subfactor. This realization of quantum $6j$-symbols differs from their realization through a flat bi-unitary connection arising from the higher relative commutants of a subfactor.
item.dc:creator: Yasuyuki Kawahigashi

item.title: Cluster Condensation and Symmetry-Protected Thermal Rigidity of Bose gases on the Haldane Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.02799v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that a spinless Bose gas on a Haldane sphere with a small monopole charge \(q\) realizes, in the lowest Landau level (LLL), an exactly solvable SU(2)-protected cluster condensate: a Hafnian condensate of two-boson singlets for \(q=1\), analogous to resonating-valence-bond singlet coverings, and a four-boson singlet condensate for \(q=3/2\). Unlike topologically protected quantum Hall states, the exactness of these states relies only on SU(2) symmetry and repulsiveness, with no pseudopotential fine-tuning. Their SU(2)-protected degeneracy renders the single-particle correlations exactly temperature-independent even as the clusters dissociate, a thermal rigidity absent in conventional Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs). Increasing the interaction drives a transition to a vortex BEC with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Meng-Jie Wang, Jun-Hui Zheng

item.title: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.02841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.
item.dc:creator: M. Cristina Diamantini, Carlo A. Trugenberger

item.title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
item.description: arXiv:2611.03207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. A resource estimate shows that a quantum advantage for the ground state could appear only for dots of about 15 to 21 qubits or more. There, a single Trotter step already requires two-qubit error rates of order 10^{-6}, beyond the reach of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. We test the assumptions of this estimate with an imaginary-time matrix product state (MPS) that applies each dot as one block. It agrees with exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2). At (5, 2), a variational circuit with the same dot-plus-link layout comes within 3.6% of the exact energy, and noisy simulations show that its fidelity decays as assumed in the resource estimate. At (8, 5), i.e., N = 40 qubits, the energy converges at bond dimension chi = 768, far below the exact value 2^20, and the inter-dot entanglement stays small and is set mainly by K. Out-of-time-order correlators across the links decay on a time scale that shrinks rapidly with |K|. Thus, the dot size p and the inter-dot coupling K together set the entanglement of the chain, and with it where a quantum advantage could appear.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Dey, Abel Carreras, Siddhartha Patra

item.title: From photons to fractons: Casimir effect in higher-rank electrodynamics and its fractonic branch
item.description: arXiv:2611.03269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Casimir effect probes the modes that can propagate between boundaries. This makes it useful for fracton gauge theories, where restricted mobility follows from the simultaneous conservation of charge and dipole moment and changes the physical sector of the theory. We compare ordinary Maxwell electrodynamics with a Lorentz-covariant higher-rank theory of a symmetric tensor gauge field and with the scalar-charge fractonic branch selected from it by a preferred timelike background. The comparison shows why the distinction matters. In the full covariant theory, the Euclidean slab problem contains three independently propagating Maxwell-like modes and two coupled vector sectors that do not reduce to independent ordinary modes. Their boundary determinants are well defined, but a Lorentzian analysis shows that the vector sector has an unbounded Hamiltonian, so these determinants do not describe the vacuum energy of a stable fractonic phase. On the fractonic branch, the Gauss constraint removes that vector sector and leaves three stable massless modes: two transverse-traceless tensor modes and one scalar trace mode. For ideal reflectors, the physical Casimir energy is therefore 3/2 of the corresponding Maxwell result, for both equal and complementary boundary conditions. The calculation isolates the effect of the fractonic restriction on the radiative spectrum and clarifies which features of the full higher-rank boundary problem survive in the physical fracton sector.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Maggiore

item.title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic R\'enyi defects
item.description: arXiv:2611.03413v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The R\'enyi entropies of a ball are computed by a conformal defect, the R\'enyi defect, dual in holography to a hyperbolic black hole. At an index $n_*$ its charged operator merges with its alternate-quantization partner, and the defect loses conformality. Beyond $n_*$ it flows with no source to a conformal defect that breaks the U(1) symmetry; below $n_*$ that defect needs a symmetry-breaking source, so at large $N$, conformality loss makes the breaking spontaneous. The scalar hair beyond $n_*$, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, thus preserves them outside a thin layer at the entangling surface, as conformal symmetry requires. The region outside the layer sets the universal term of the R\'enyi entropy. We demonstrate the mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, where the saddles are in closed form and numerical methods confirm the flows. On a sphere we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the sphere is large enough; it is then unique and ends at the symmetry-breaking defect. The mechanism needs a scalar mass in a finite window, and for potentials attractive at small amplitude, the symmetry can break before conformality is lost. For operators of low enough dimension, already the second R\'enyi entropy lies beyond the merger. Classical backreaction does not move the merger at any order; we argue that away from $n_*$ the flows persist at first order.
item.dc:creator: Siqing Yu

item.title: The Virasoro Bootstrap: from the $c\sim1$ desert to coupled Potts
item.description: arXiv:2611.03565v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a numerical conformal bootstrap for two-dimensional CFTs with $c>1$ based on Virasoro conformal blocks, computed with Zamolodchikov's recursion and optimal polynomial interpolation. As a first test we isolate an island around three decoupled Ising models. We then consider three 3-state Potts models coupled through their energy operators, a candidate irrational CFT. Mixed correlators isolate the decoupled theory in an island, and different gap assumptions, motivated by perturbation theory, yield a peninsula that contains the coupled fixed point but not the decoupled one. Finally, we explore the standard single-correlator bound on the lowest-dimension scalar primary in the OPE of two identical scalars. We find that for central charges just above $c=1$ the bound collapses over a wide range of external dimensions. This excludes any theory whose lightest scalar is absent from its own OPE and lies in this range, and supports the conjecture that no compact CFT exists in this region. We explain several features of these bounds analytically.
item.dc:creator: Stefanos R. Kousvos, Alessandro Piazza, Alessandro Vichi

item.title: Long-range model for electronic pseudospin-nuclear-spin coupling and two-stage ordering in TmVO$_4$
item.description: arXiv:2507.16619v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an infinite-range coupled electronic-pseudospin and nuclear-spin model for ferroquadrupolar and nuclear-spin ordering in TmVO$_4$ in external magnetic and strain fields. This material is an experimental realization of a transverse-field Ising model, where the Ising degree of freedom is quadrupolar and non-magnetic, but a transverse component is magnetic and couples both to external magnetic fields and to the nuclear spins via a hyperfine coupling. At zero external magnetic field, the electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom undergo well-separated two-stage ordering, accompanied by the release of their respective entropies. A transverse magnetic field polarizes the electronic orbital moments and, via the hyperfine coupling, the nuclear spins. The quadrupolar ordering temperature is gradually reduced to zero. However, the nuclear transition is replaced by a crossover at nonzero magnetic field. Quantum fluctuations are enhanced near the phase transitions and lead to peaks in the magnetic susceptibility. The spectral functions reveal a softening of a low-energy mode near the quantum critical point, consistent with the closing of the excitation gap and its reopening in the disordered phase. These features provide direct dynamical signatures of the field-driven quantum critical phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Ghosh, Anirudha Menon, Manoranjan Kumar, Rajiv R. P. Singh

item.title: Emergent Gauge Flux in Mixed QED$_3$ with Flavor Chemical Potential: Implications for Magnetized U(1) Dirac Spin Liquids
item.description: arXiv:2508.08528v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We design a lattice model of a "mixed" U(1) gauge field coupled to fermions with a flavor chemical potential and solve it with large-scale determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations. In this mixed construction, dynamical magnetic monopole events are suppressed in the temporal-continuum limit. For zero flavor chemical potential, the model realizes three-dimensional quantum electrodynamics (QED$_3$) which has been argued to describe the ground state and low-energy excitations of the Dirac spin liquid phase of quantum antiferromagnets. At finite flavor chemical potential, which corresponds to a Zeeman field perturbing the Dirac spin liquid, we find a "chiral flux" phase which is characterized by the generation of a finite mean emergent gauge flux and, accordingly, the formation of relativistic Landau levels for the Dirac fermions. We use field-theory arguments to argue that in this state a U(1)$_m$ magnetic symmetry is spontaneously broken, leading to a gapless photon mode. Because of spin-flux attachment this mode would contribute to the low-energy longitudinal spin response. We numerically compute longitudinal and transverse spin structure factors which match our continuum and lattice mean-field theory predictions. In a different region of the phase diagram, strong fluctuations of the emergent gauge field give rise to an antiferromagnetically ordered state with gapped Dirac fermions coexisting with a deconfined gauge field. We also find an interesting intermediate phase where the chiral flux phase and the antiferromagnetic phase coexist. We argue that our results pave the way to testable predictions for magnetized Dirac spin liquids in frustrated quantum antiferromagnets.
item.dc:creator: Chuang Chen, Urban F. P. Seifert, Kexin Feng, Oleg A. Starykh, Leon Balents, Zi Yang Meng

item.title: Symmetry-Protected Topological Structures in Quantum Many-Body Scar Subspaces
item.description: arXiv:2512.11216v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate how symmetry-associated topological properties, originally defined for ground states, can be consistently extended to dynamically isolated subspaces of quantum many-body systems. Focusing on quantum many-body scars (QMBS), we show that a scar subspace is invariant under the relevant symmetries, and it can support well-defined topological properties inherited from an underlying symmetry-protected topological (SPT) ground state, even though individual scar states need not themselves be symmetric. We refer to such structures as SPT-like scar subspaces, emphasizing that the topological properties are defined at the level of the symmetry-invariant subspace rather than on a state-by-state basis. As a concrete example, we analyze the spin-$1$ Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki (AKLT) model, where a restricted spectrum-generating algebra (rSGA) generates a tower of QMBS on top of a nontrivial SPT ground state admitting a matrix product state (MPS) representation. We demonstrate that the resulting symmetry-invariant scar subspace inherits well-defined topological characteristics, encoded in bond-space symmetry representations, expectation values of symmetry-twist operators, and long-range string order in the dilute regime. We further show that these features persist in a broader class of models, including deformations and higher-spin generalizations that preserve the relevant symmetries and admit nontrivial SPT ground states with MPS representations. Our results provide a general framework in which symmetry-associated topological properties, while inherited from the ground state, are consistently realized at the level of symmetry-invariant nonthermal subspaces. This perspective clarifies how topological structures can be meaningfully defined beyond individual eigenstates.
item.dc:creator: Chihiro Matsui, Thomas Quella, Naoto Tsuji

item.title: Non-invertible symmetries and mixed anomalies from equations of motion in (3+1)D twisted $BF$ topological quantum field theories
item.description: arXiv:2601.01523v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a systematic study on the topological operators that generate invertible and non-invertible higher-form symmetries in $\left(3+1\right)D$ twisted $BF$ topological quantum field theories (TQFTs). We focus on the twisted $BF$ theories with gauge group $G=\prod_i \mathbb{Z}_{N_i}$ and an $a\wedge a\wedge b$ twist, where $a$'s and $b$ are 1-form and 2-form gauge fields, respectively. These theories realize non-Abelian $(3+1)$D TQFTs supporting Borromean-Rings braiding and describe three-dimensional non-Abelian topological orders in condensed matter. For $G=(\mathbb{Z}_2)^3$, a microscopic realization is given by the $\mathbb{D}_4$ Kitaev quantum double model. Starting from the equations of motion (EoMs), we construct gauge invariant operators that are supported on closed submanifolds, hence are genuine topological operators. Some of them are associated with nontrivial Hilbert spaces which are the projective representation spaces of specific gauge subgroups, thus being non-invertible. The others are invertible topological operators with group-like fusion rules. The fusion rules of non-invertible topological operators correspond to the decomposition of the product of the projective representation spaces. We provide a field-theoretical algorithm to calculate the fusion rules. Besides, we identify an obstruction to retaining a non-invertible topological operator after gauging an invertible symmetry, and derive the constraints on pairs of non-invertible operators relevant to simultaneous gauging. Our results give a unified and practical approach for identifying and characterizing higher-form symmetries and mixed anomalies, which can be extended to more general TQFTs and topological orders.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Feng Zhang, Yizhou Huang, Qing-Rui Wang, Peng Ye

item.title: Circular dichroism in second- and third-harmonic generation in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi
item.description: arXiv:2604.03983v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We theoretically investigate circular dichroism (CD) in second- and third-harmonic generation (SHG and THG) in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi. We demonstrate that both SHG and THG exhibit dichroic responses of order unity, while their robustness against spectral broadening is strikingly different. Specifically, while SHG-CD is strongly suppressed by dissipation, THG-CD remains robust over a wide frequency range. We show that this qualitative difference originates from the phase structure of the nonlinear current, where SHG-CD arises from subleading interference processes that are sensitive to dephasing, whereas THG-CD emerges already at the leading nonlinear order and is therefore protected against spectral broadening. As a result, THG-CD provides a robust probe of chirality encoded in nonequilibrium electronic dynamics. We further reveal non-monotonic frequency dependences and pronounced sensitivity of harmonic emission to the polarization state and crystallographic orientation of the driving field. Our results provide a representative example of robust nonlinear chiroptical responses in chiral topological semimetals and highlight the potential of high-harmonic spectroscopy as a probe of phase-resolved electronic dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Yuya Ominato, Masahito Mochizuki

item.title: Replica Tensor Train
item.description: arXiv:2604.22718v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe a numerical many-body technique that is based on both tensor networks and quantum Monte Carlo. The variational ansatz is a tensor network that can harvest volume-law entanglement. It is constructed from a tensor train to which one applies a set of non-local operators that force several indices of the tensor train to represent the same physical index, hence its name -- replica tensor train (RTT). From the tensor network toolbox, it inherits the possibility to make linear combinations of these states and apply a certain class of operators. We can therefore find the ground-state of a local Hamiltonian in a purely algebraic way as in standard tensor network algorithms -- i.e. without using gradient descent methods. On the other hand, the volume-law structure forbids calculating physical observables directly. In much the same way as on a quantum computer where one can prepare a state but can only sample it at the end, here we have to use Markov Chain Monte Carlo to compute the observables. We further show that the approach can be extended to build Krylov-subspace ground-state methods within the variational manifold. We illustrate the different algorithms on a two-dimensional spin model with a transverse magnetic field, which can be solved by this approach at low computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Miha Srdinsek, Gabriel Gouraud, Xavier Waintal

item.title: Constructing Bulk Topological Orders via Layered Gauging
item.description: arXiv:2604.27363v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding quantum phases and phase transitions in the presence of symmetries is a central objective of quantum many-body physics. A powerful modern paradigm for investigating this problem is topological holography, which relates symmetries in $k$ dimensions to "bulk" topological orders in $(k+1)$ dimensions. While conceptually profound, most existing bulk construction methods rely on sophisticated mathematical formalisms and can be difficult to apply to certain symmetry types. In this work, we propose a physically intuitive and versatile method, termed the layered gauging construction, to systematically generate $(k+1)$-dimensional (liquid or fracton) topological orders from $k$-dimensional generalized symmetries. Roughly speaking, the prescription is to stack many layers of $k$-dimensional quantum systems with certain symmetries into a $(k+1)$-dimensional pile, and then sequentially gauge a diagonal symmetry acting on each nearest-neighbor pair of layers. The detailed procedure depends on the specific symmetry types. We have successfully implemented the method in a number of examples in different spatial dimensions, with symmetries that are conventional, higher-form, subsystem, anomalous, nonabelian, or noninvertible. We hence conjecture the method to be very general. For example, from the subsystem symmetry of the $2d$ plaquette Ising model, we derive the X-cube model and also an anisotropic fracton topological order. Additionally, starting from an anomalous $Z_2$ symmetry in $1d$, we construct a new square lattice model realizing the double semion topological order. From a quantum-error-correction perspective, our layered gauging construction may be viewed as a generalization of the hypergraph-product construction beyond the standard Calderbank-Shor-Steane setting.
item.dc:creator: Shang Liu

item.title: Band Structure and topology of a periodically deformed Kitaev honeycomb model
item.description: arXiv:2605.20181v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the growing interest in spin liquids and topological phases, as well as the rise of deformation engineering, we study the combined effects of deformation and magnetic fields on the honeycomb Kitaev model. The Kitaev model, as one of the prototypical and exactly solvable spin liquid-hosting models, serves as a simple platform that demonstrates the rich physics one can expect at the intersection of deformation physics and quantum spin liquids. Our work builds on a simplified solution to the undeformed base model that we present. This simplified solution allows for a straightforward extension of our analysis to the deformed case. After incorporating periodic deformations into the Kitaev model (chosen for its similarity to moir\'e physics), we investigate the effects of a hexagonally symmetric deformation on the band structure. We find that deformation leads to a smaller Brillouin zone with new band gaps at the edges, indicating the potential for topological transitions. Finally, we introduce a magnetic field to break time-reversal symmetry and thereby allow for non-trivial topology. We find that, under specific parameter conditions, the magnetic field leads to multiple band-gap closings and openings. An investigation into topological properties reveals nontrivial Chern numbers and a plethora of topological transitions. The resulting nontrivial band topology may motivate future investigations of thermal Hall or related transverse responses, which are not calculated here. We also propose a bulk-measurement approach to the Chern numbers and a possible path to their physical realization. Most importantly, our results demonstrate the rich phenomenology that can arise from the interplay between deformation and spin-liquid physics.
item.dc:creator: Abdullah AlJishi, Ali AlSwaid, Moayad Ekhwan, Hocine Bahlouli, Raditya Weda Bomantara, Michael Vogl

item.title: Magnon bandstructure and topology in a periodically deformed Kagome lattice with DM interaction
item.description: arXiv:2606.00696v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the band structure and topology of magnons for a Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction on a deformed Kagome lattice. For simplicity, we focus on a periodically deformed lattice with hexagonal symmetry and an enlarged unit cell. This enlarged unit cell gives rise to a more complex band structure than in the undeformed case. Analyzing band topology, there is a distinction between the topologically trivial case with anti-ferromagnetic coupling and the topologically non-trivial case with ferromagnetic coupling. In the anti-ferromagnetic case, a spin-space symmetry, also present in the classical ground state, enforces these topologically trivial states. In the ferromagnetic case, this symmetry is spontaneously broken by the classical ground state. Consequently, the band structure also hosts numerous topological features. Specifically, we observe many topological transitions and bands with Chern numbers ranging from $+2$ to $-2$, which makes the system richer than in the undeformed case. This emergent topological structure demonstrates that deformed magnets can host new and exciting physics.
item.dc:creator: Mohammed Abdullah Hammadi, Mohammed Salman Alsadah, Husam Abdulmajeed Noorwli, Hocine Bahlouli, Michael Vogl

item.title: Unconventional Mixed-Parity Magnetism in Rare-Earth Tetraborides
item.description: arXiv:2607.02117v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Altermagnetism has advanced the study of compensated magnets by revealing non-relativistic spin splitting, traditionally classified into strictly even- or odd-parity spin textures. Here, we establish component-resolved mixed-parity spin splitting in a fully three-dimensional compensated magnet and identify its microscopic origin. Using first-principles calculations, tight-binding and $\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{p}$ models, along with spin-group symmetry analysis, we demonstrate that the non-coplanar ground state of $\mathrm{TbB}_4$ enforces odd-parity $p$- and $f$-wave-like textures for the in-plane spin components while the out-of-plane component retains an even-parity $d$-wave altermagnetic character. Crucially, the $p$-wave texture is driven not by relativistic spin-orbit coupling but by a staggered emergent flux arising from the scalar spin chirality of the non-coplanar order. This mixed-parity structure dictates distinct transport fingerprints, including bulk non-relativistic Edelstein and spin Hall responses that respond characteristically to reversal of the chirality domains. Spin-orbit coupling additionally enables a Berry curvature dipole. These results establish the rare-earth tetraborides as a robust platform for engineering complex spin-charge conversion phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Dong-Choon Ryu, Jae-Ho Han, Bongjae Kim, Chang-Jong Kang

item.title: Spinless Charged Excitation at the Interface between a Conventional Topological Insulator and a Topological Mott Insulator
item.description: arXiv:2607.14221v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the interface separating two topologically distinct insulating phases of matter using extensive density-matrix renormalization group calculations to study the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model with a spatially varying interaction strength, chosen to realize both integer quantum Hall and chiral spin liquid states in different spatial regions. We find that the integer quantum Hall-chiral spin liquid interface hosts a spinless charged excitation that is bound to the interface. This mode at the interface is identified through charge and spin pumping, and by direct calculations of low-lying excited states. We also characterize bulk excitations in both phases, finding evidence for fractionalization in the chiral spin liquid and for spin-triplet exciton formation in the integer quantum Hall phase.
item.dc:creator: Cesar A. Gallegos, Andrew J. Millis, Steven R. White

item.title: Differentiable Inverse Design of Two-Body Interactions for the Moore-Read State
item.description: arXiv:2607.23695v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Designing interactions that stabilize target quantum states is a central challenge in strongly correlated physics. For fractional quantum Hall states, identifying suitable two-body interactions remains difficult even when a target wave function is known. Here we implement a differentiable inverse-design approach that combines automatic differentiation with exact diagonalization to optimize two-body interactions, using the Moore--Read Pfaffian state as a benchmark. The optimized ground states achieve overlaps exceeding 99\% with the target for systems containing up to 12 electrons. Excitation and entanglement spectra provide complementary finite-size diagnostics. A common exponential pseudopotential profile retains an overlap of 91.1\% at 14 electrons without further optimization, supporting its transferability beyond the optimization sizes. These results demonstrate the approach on a non-Abelian quantum Hall benchmark and motivate its application to other numerically accessible trial states for which suitable approximate parent Hamiltonians remain unknown.
item.dc:creator: Yi Yang, Xin Wan, Zi-Xiang Hu

item.title: Spin splitting without symmetry: a nearly compensated ferrimagnet and the origin of altermagnetism
item.description: arXiv:2609.12931v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The spin splitting of collinear altermagnets is usually attributed to the crystal symmetry relating the opposite-spin sublattices --- a rotation or mirror in place of the translation or inversion of a conventional antiferromagnet. We show that this symmetry organizes the splitting but does not produce it; its origin is the anisotropic arrangement of the magnetic orbitals and their ligands, which also fixes the symmetry itself. Two results establish this. A triclinic ($P1$) \ce{Mn} oxide, a fully compensated ferrimagnet whose two inequivalent sublattices are related by no symmetry, is spin split throughout the Brillouin zone; repositioning the same ligands, atom for atom, to restore an inversion centre relating the two metal sites collapses the splitting to a residual two orders of magnitude smaller, so the splitting follows from the arrangement rather than the symmetry. Symmetry, we show formally, can only ever reverse or forbid a splitting that already exists: it cannot create one between sublattices an arrangement has left electronically identical, nor where the underlying orbitals carry no anisotropy to arrange in the first place. Organizing the analysis through an operation-resolved symmetry hierarchy and reading the crystal classes as a single axis, the enforced nodal planes fall from two to one to zero across the orthorhombic, monoclinic, and triclinic classes while the arrangement-generated splitting persists to the base. The altermagnet and the fully compensated ferrimagnet are thus the two ends of one axis --- the same splitting, organized by symmetry at one end and unorganized at the other --- and the search for compensated spin-split magnets is a search over orbital arrangements rather than symmetry labels.
item.dc:creator: Jaekyung Jang, Joo Yull Rhee

item.title: Lyapunov-controlled thermalization: an exact real-time example
item.description: arXiv:2609.20597v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A verified Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) relation, after a drive has ceased, is not sufficient evidence to prove equilibrium. We demonstrate this in a large-$N$ large-$q$ Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) quench protocol. Although all post-quench fermion correlators are exactly thermal, a second quench back to the initial Hamiltonian reveals hidden memory of the initial state. It is encoded in correlators connecting to times before the first quench. This memory is an extensive nonequilibrium (NEQ) witness with its decay rate being the Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_L$. Thus $\lambda_L$ sets the rate at which the state becomes effectively indistinguishable from a Gibbs state. Despite being a unitary interacting many-body system, the complete NEQ real-time evolution is obtained exactly in the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, making the setup ideal for analytically studying thermalization.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Loy, Jan C. Louw

item.title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
item.description: arXiv:2610.34470v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Bellomia, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera, Massimo Capone, Adriano Amaricci

item.title: New horizons for inhomogeneous quenches and Floquet CFT
item.description: arXiv:2404.07884v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A fruitful avenue in investigating out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is to abruptly change their Hamiltonian and study the subsequent evolution of their quantum state. If this is done once, the setup is called a quench, while if it is done periodically, it is called Floquet driving. We consider the solvable setup of a two-dimensional CFT driven by Hamiltonians built out of conformal symmetry generators: in this case, the quantum dynamics can be understood using two-dimensional geometry. We investigate how the dynamics is reflected in the holographic dual three-dimensional spacetime and find new horizons. We argue that bulk operators behind the new horizons are reconstructable by virtue of modular flow.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhi Jiang, M\'ark Mezei

item.title: The entanglement membrane in 2d CFT: reflected entropy, RG flow, and information velocity
item.description: arXiv:2411.16542v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The time evolution of entanglement entropy in generic chaotic many-body systems has an effective description in terms of a minimal membrane, characterised by a tension function. For 2d CFTs, a degenerate tension function reproduces several results regarding the dynamics of the entropy; this stands in contrast to higher dimensions where the tension is non-degenerate. In this paper we use holography to show that, in order to correctly capture the reflected entropy in 2d CFT, one needs to add an additional degree of freedom to the membrane description. Furthermore, we show that the conventional non-degenerate membrane tension function emerges upon introducing a relevant deformation of the CFT, dual to a planar BTZ black hole with scalar hair and with an interior Kasner universe. Finally, we also study the membrane description for reflected entropy and information velocity arXiv:1908.06993 in higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhi Jiang, M\'ark Mezei, Julio Virrueta

item.title: Polarons in atomic gases and two-dimensional semiconductors
item.description: arXiv:2501.09618v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we provide a comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental studies of the properties of polarons formed by mobile impurities strongly interacting with quantum many-body systems. We present a unified perspective on the universal concepts and theoretical techniques used to characterize polarons in two distinct platforms, ultracold atomic gases and atomically-thin transition metal dichalcogenides, which are linked by many deep parallels. We review polarons in both fermionic and bosonic environments, highlighting their similarities and differences including the intricate interplay between few- and many-body physics. Various kinds of polarons with long-range interactions or in magnetic backgrounds are discussed, and the theoretical and experimental progress towards understanding interactions between polarons is described. We outline how polaron physics, regarded as the low density limit of quantum mixtures, provides fundamental insights regarding the phase diagram of complex condensed matter systems. Furthermore, we describe how polarons may serve as quantum sensors of many-body physics in complex environments. Our work highlights the open problems, identifies new research directions and provides a comprehensive framework for this rapidly evolving research field.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Massignan, Richard Schmidt, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Ata\c{c} \.Imamoglu, Martin Zwierlein, Jan J. Arlt, Georg M. Bruun

item.title: Free mutual information and higher-point OTOCs
item.description: arXiv:2509.13406v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a quantity called the free mutual information (FMI), adapted from concepts in free probability theory, as a new physical measure of quantum chaos. This quantity captures the spreading of a time-evolved operator in the space of all possible operators on the Hilbert space, which is doubly exponential in the number of degrees of freedom. It thus provides a finer notion of operator spreading than the well-understood phenomenon of operator growth in physical space. We derive two central results which apply in any physical system: first, an explicit "Coulomb gas" formula for the FMI of two observables $A(t)$ and $B$ in terms of the eigenvalues of the product operator $A(t)B$; and second, a general relation expressing the FMI as a weighted sum of all higher-point out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs). This second result provides a precise information-theoretic interpretation for the higher-point OTOCs as collectively quantifying operator ergodicity and the approach to freeness. This physical interpretation is particularly useful in light of recent progress in experimentally measuring higher-point OTOCs. We identify universal behaviours of the FMI and higher-point OTOCs across a variety of chaotic systems, including random unitary circuits and chaotic spin chains, which indicate that spreading in the doubly exponential operator space is a generic feature of quantum many-body chaos. At the same time, the non-generic behavior of the FMI in various non-chaotic systems, including certain unitary designs, shows that there are cases where an operator spreads in physical space but remains localized in operator space. The FMI is thus a sharper diagnostic of chaos than the standard 4-point OTOC.
item.dc:creator: Shreya Vardhan, Jinzhao Wang

item.title: Time Evolution of Multi-Party Entanglement Signals
item.description: arXiv:2511.16729v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the real-time dynamics of multi-party entanglement signals in chaotic quantum many-body systems including but not necessarily restricted to holographic conformal field theories. We find that scrambling dynamics generates multiparty entanglement with rich structure including: (a) qualitatively different dynamical behaviours for different signals, likely reflecting different dynamics for different kinds of entanglement patterns, (b) discontinuities indicating dynamical phase transitions in the entanglement structure, (c) transient and non-monotonic multiparty entanglement, and (d) periods during which the extensive entanglement of some regions is entirely multipartite. Our main technical tool is the membrane theory of entanglement dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Vijay Balasubramanian, Hanzhi Jiang, Simon F. Ross

item.title: Nonreciprocal perfect Coulomb drag in electron-hole bilayers: coherent exciton superflow as a diode
item.description: arXiv:2602.02643v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Distinguishing an exciton condensate from an excitonic gas or insulator remains a fundamental challenge, as both phases feature bound electron-hole pairs but differ only by the emergence of macroscopic phase coherence. Here, we theoretically propose that a spin-orbit-coupled bilayer system can host a finite-momentum exciton condensate exhibiting a nonreciprocal perfect Coulomb drag -- the coherent-exciton diode effect. This effect arises from the simultaneous breaking of inversion and time-reversal symmetries in the exciton condensate, resulting in direction-dependent critical counterflow currents. The resulting nonreciprocal perfect Coulomb drag provides a clear and unambiguous transport signature of phase-coherent exciton condensation, offering a powerful and experimentally accessible approach to identify, probe, and control exciton superfluidity in solid-state platforms.
item.dc:creator: Jun-Xiao Hui, Qing-Dong Jiang

item.title: Bayesian phase transition for the critical Ising model: Enlarged replica symmetry in the epsilon expansion and in 2D
item.description: arXiv:2604.23346v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A process that images or measures bond energies in the critical Ising model can be in distinct measurement 'phases', depending on the precision of measurement. We study the transition into the strong-measurement phase using replica field theory (an epsilon expansion around six dimensions), a symmetry analysis, and numerical simulations in two dimensions. The results show that certain inference problems possess unexpected structure associated with an enlarged symmetry of the replica description. The symmetry imposes constraints on correlation functions, and is an analog of the Nishimori phenomenon in the Ising spin glass, but in a distinct replica limit. It determines the exact critical exponent for an Edwards-Anderson-like correlator in the measured Ising model, both in 2D and near the upper critical dimension. The symmetry is present microscopically for certain measurement protocols, and it emerges in the infrared for generic protocols at the critical measurement strength. We also examine the epsilon expansion for models with power-law interactions and/or long-range measurement. Finally, we describe an analogous replica symmetry enlargement for measurement in Wegner's lattice gauge theory.
item.dc:creator: Kay Joerg Wiese, Alapan Das, Adam Nahum

item.title: Computing eigenpairs of quantum many-body systems with Polfed.jl
item.description: arXiv:2605.10191v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present Polfed$.$jl, an open-source Julia package implementing the Polynomially Filtered Exact Diagonalization (POLFED) algorithm for computing mid-spectrum eigenvalues and eigenvectors (shortly, eigenpairs) of quantum many-body Hamiltonians. Access to such eigenpairs is essential for studying non-equilibrium many-body physics, but is hindered by the exponential growth of Hilbert-space dimension. POLFED addresses this challenge through a polynomial spectral transformation evaluated on the fly within a Lanczos iteration, preserving Hamiltonian sparsity and substantially reducing memory costs compared to other diagonalization methods. The package supports flexible energy targeting, automatic optimization of the spectral mapping for structured Hamiltonians, and GPU acceleration, which is particularly effective since the dominant computational cost reduces to repeated sparse matrix-vector multiplications. Benchmarks on disordered spin-chain and fermionic models demonstrate access to larger system sizes than alternative approaches, and CPU--GPU comparisons confirm significant speedups. In particular, we also provide code for constructing the quantum sun model Hamiltonian, a toy model of a many-body ergodicity-breaking transition. While our focus is on many-body Hamiltonians, Polfed$.$jl may be applied to any large sparse matrix.
item.dc:creator: Rok Pintar, Konrad Pawlik, Rafa{\l} \'Swi\k{e}tek, Miroslav Hopjan, Jan \v{S}untajs, Jakub Zakrzewski, Piotr Sierant, Lev Vidmar

item.title: Helical Domain-Wall-Ring Networks Reshape Superconducting Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2606.23599v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Extended domain-wall networks that emerge in moir\'e materials provide a distinct platform for quasi-one-dimensional electronic states. However, the interaction-driven orders in confined networks remain largely unexplored. Here, we discuss superconducting (SC) correlations in interacting helical domain-wall-ring networks in the closed topological domains formed within the moir\'e patterns of an underlying twisted bilayer honeycomb lattice. We first analyze the system within the framework of an infinite-size theory and show that inter-ring SC-pair tunneling is renormalization-group relevant in an appropriate interaction regime, favoring enhanced SC correlations through inter-ring phase locking. To address finite-size effects resulting from the ring-network geometry, we present a self-consistent variational approach. Our analysis shows that even in the regime where the infinite-size theory predicts strongly coupled pair tunneling, the induced phase-locking scale remains strongly suppressed. In contrast, the SC scaling dimension is governed mainly by density-density interactions and ring geometry, decreasing modestly with decreasing twist angle while remaining insensitive to the pair-tunneling strength. This discrepancy demonstrates that ring networks cannot generally be understood as simple finite-size truncations of their infinite-size counterparts but can exhibit qualitatively distinct collective behavior. Our study highlights how the interplay of confinement effects and ring-network geometry can reshape SC correlations.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Chun Hung, Arun Bansil

item.title: Thermal Hall tomography of superconducting topology in rhombohedral graphene
item.description: arXiv:2608.12586v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Chiral superconductors should carry Majorana modes along their edges, yet three decades of work on candidate materials have not measured the integer that counts them. Rhombohedral graphene offers a new route, because its superconductivity coexists with magnetic domains that can be imaged and rewritten. Here we show how heat transport can read this integer and test it against the domain pattern. Warping and finite pair momentum can close the excitation gap while the band Chern number stays fixed. An exact two-band thermal kernel shows how quantization is then lost and bounds the plateau error when the gap survives. Real-space calculations with disorder show that the integer survives disorder several times larger than the gap, because a mobility gap remains. Bogoliubov pockets instead turn the bulk into a heat conductor, and disorder does not restore quantization. Time-reversed domains should show opposite plateaux, and with ideal contacts a wall between them should carry twice either plateau. In microscopic calculations, a written wall carries this number of Majorana channels even when its core is metallic. Writing, moving and erasing such walls would test superconducting topology, its link to magnetism, and protected heat flow in one device.
item.dc:creator: Kumar Ghosh

item.title: The large $N$ vector model with angular velocity
item.description: arXiv:2608.31151v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the free energy of a critical vector model at large $N$ on $S^{1}\times S^{2}$ with an angular velocity $\hat\mu$ without the singlet constraint. We study the model for which the large $N$ dynamics is controlled by the uniform saddle point of the auxiliary field arising in the Hubbard-Stratanovich transformation. The leading high-temperature behaviour is determined analytically both as an expansion about $\hat\mu r=0$ and $\hat\mu^{2}r^{2}=1$ where $r$ is the radius of the sphere. We supplement the analytic results with a numerical analysis that agrees with both the analytical expansions in their respective regimes and smoothly interpolates between them. The leading high-temperature contribution to the free energy develops a pole at $\hat\mu^{2}r^{2}=1$, in agreement with expectations from the thermal effective field theory. Its residue coincides with that of the massless free theory. Sub-leading terms, however, exhibit non-analytic dependence on the angular velocity and distinguish the critical fixed-point result from the free theory answer. The residue at the pole can also be obtained by placing the model on the pp-wave geometry. We show that the residue agrees with that obtained from the direct computation. The free energy of the model connects the non-trivial fixed point of the $O(N)$ model at $\hat\mu r=0$ to its free fixed point at $\hat\mu^2r^2=1$.
item.dc:creator: Justin R. David, Srijan Kumar

item.title: Imaging phase winding in topological superconductors with a fork-tip Josephson STM
item.description: arXiv:2609.38174v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The topological phase winding in a chiral superconductor remains challenging to access by conventional real-space probes. We propose a scheme to probe this winding with a fork-tip Josephson STM near an impurity, where two superconducting tips form an interferometer sensitive to phase differences between two positions. The phase winding remains accessible via the fork-tip critical current even if the relative phase between the fork-tip and sample fluctuates, establishing a route towards a local phase-sensitive STM probe of topological superconductivity. We numerically compute the interference pattern to demonstrate that the magnitude and phase of the order parameter can be reconstructed as a function of angle, providing a route towards resolving the longstanding open experimental problem of directly detecting phase winding in topological superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Vladislav Poliakov, Archisman Panigrahi

item.title: Large superconducting diode effect indicates nonuniform triplet pairing in UTe2
item.description: arXiv:2610.36332v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is characterized by unequal critical current magnitudes for opposite-polarity current flow, owing to broken spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries. For a superconducting pair wavefunction to spontaneously break inversion symmetry implies the formation of Cooper pairs with nonzero momentum, yielding a nonuniform superconducting state. For singlet superconductors, the formation of such a (FFLO) state has long been understood to provide an escape from high field Pauli pair-breaking -- how and why such an effect might occur for equal spin pairing is an open question. Here we report the observation of a large SDE in bulk specimens of the three-dimensional heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe$_2$, with a peak diode efficiency of 33% at the high magnetic field strength of 33.6 T, representing the highest-field observation of the SDE to date. Crucially, this nonreciprocal transport is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state near a first-order metamagnetic phase boundary. The absence of the SDE away from this slender phase-intersection argues strongly against purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries. Instead, our findings indicate spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing. We model this behavior using a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theory, demonstrating that the intertwining of magnetic and triplet superconducting orders can stabilize an odd-parity FFLO state.
item.dc:creator: Zheyu Wu, Daniel Shaffer, Dmitry V. Chichinadze, Mengmeng Long, Hanyi Chen, Andrej Cabala, Theodore I. Weinberger, Maurice Bal, Steffen Wiedmann, Dave Graf, Vladimir Sechovsk\'y, Michal Vali\v{s}ka, F. Malte Grosche, Alex Levchenko, Alexander G. Eaton

item.title: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies
item.description: arXiv:2610.37745v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ordinary $0$-form symmetries $G$ can mix with $1$-form symmetries $\Pi_2$ to form a $2$-group $\mathcal{G}$. We give a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite $2$-group symmetries in terms of local relations among symmetry operators. These relations identify the Postnikov class $[\rho]\in H^3(BG,\Pi_2)$ that characterizes the mixing. We develop a method to extract anomalies of these symmetries in one spatial dimension by restricting symmetry operations to an interval and comparing their composition near its endpoints. We also construct explicit qubit symmetry actions in $d=1,2,3$ spatial dimensions for a $2$-group with $G=\Pi_2=\mathbb{Z}_2$. These actions share the same nontrivial Postnikov class but include both anomaly-free and anomalous realizations. Their cohomological anomalies are classified by $H^{d+2}(B\mathcal G,U(1))$, which is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=1,2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=3$, and our constructions realize every class in these dimensions. Our results connect higher-group symmetry and its anomalies to concrete lattice operations, providing a microscopic framework for studying anomalous symmetries.
item.dc:creator: Yitao Feng, Yu-An Chen

item.title: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and R\'enyi entropies
item.description: arXiv:2610.40371v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$, in the probe limit, is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. When the scalar mass saturates the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling takes the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase can be found in closed form on every static, uncharged AdS$_5$ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is linearly stable, as is any nodeless probe-limit condensate in the standard quantization with a nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On each slicing it answers a different question about the dual conformal field theory. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below $T_c$: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and the attenuation of sound are found in closed form. In global AdS$_5$ it describes a state of charge $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$, arguably the lowest-energy one, and gives its scaling dimension in closed form at all $Q$, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers that the superfluid effective theory does not describe; they come from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector. The hyperbolic slicing gives in closed form a homogeneous hairy phase of the black holes that compute the charged R\'enyi entropies of a ball. Its condensate does not vanish at the entangling surface. When sourced by operators inserted there, the phase sets in at R\'enyi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar.
item.dc:creator: Siqing Yu
